---
title: "Fair Learning"
---

Guide a model's learning to avoid a specific bias.  The idea is simple and it
closes the loop with [Chapter 1](../dependence/index.qmd): **fairness is
minimizing a dependence measure.**  Once you can *measure* how much two things
move together, you can add that measure to the loss and *remove* the part you
are not allowed to keep.

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## The Spine — One Objective

Every method in this chapter is the same optimization with a different
dependence term:

$$
\text{loss} \;=\; \underbrace{\text{fit}(\hat y, y)}_{\text{predict well}}
\;+\; \mu \cdot \underbrace{\operatorname{Dep}(\hat y, S)}_{\text{stay blind to } S}.
$$

Predict the target $y$ while keeping the predictions $\hat y$ independent of a
**sensitive / nuisance variable** $S$.  The weight $\mu$ dials the trade-off.
Every rung below is a *choice of* $\operatorname{Dep}$ and a way to minimize it.
:::

## Two Framings, One Operation

"Don't discriminate" and "don't load on the factor I'm hedging" are the same
maths:

| Framing | $S$ is… | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| **Fairness** | a protected attribute (sex, race, age) | predictions don't depend on $S$ |
| **Factor-neutrality** | a market/sector factor (beta) | a strategy doesn't load on $S$ |

A credit model that must not depend on `sex` and a strategy that must be
beta-neutral are solving *one* problem: remove the dependence between an output
and a variable you have chosen to be blind to.

## Why It Sits Here

- Fairness = *minimizing a dependence measure* — it reuses
  [HSIC / CKA](../dependence/02-kernels-hsic.qmd) from the dependence chapter as
  a trainable penalty.
- The "assume vs. learn the density" fork from Chapter 1 reappears: kernel
  removal needs no density; information-theoretic removal does and reconnects to
  [Gaussianization](../gaussianization/index.qmd).
- **Code:** [keras-fairkl](https://github.com/jejjohnson/keras-fairkl) — fair
  kernel learning in Keras 3, where the penalty weight is exactly this $\mu$.

## The Ladder of Removal

Each rung cancels a *shape* of dependence — mirroring the measurement ladder of
Chapter 1, now run in reverse to *remove* rather than measure.

| Rung | Method | $\operatorname{Dep}$ | Removes | Leaves |
|------|--------|------|---------|--------|
| 1 | Drop the feature | — | nothing (proxies leak) | all of it |
| 2 | Linear neutrality | `cka_linear` | the straight line | the curve |
| 3 | CKA penalty | `cka_rbf` | line **and** curve | ~nothing |
| 4 | Information removal | MI / total corr. | any shape (via density) | ~nothing |
| 5 | Adversarial | learned probe | whatever a net can find | depends |

## Pages in This Chapter

1. **[What is fair learning?](01-what-is-fair.qmd)** — the objective, the
   Lagrangian behind it, regulation (GDPR, EU AI Act), and the credit /
   factor-neutrality use cases.
2. **[Bias and proxies](02-bias-and-proxies.qmd)** — why dropping the sensitive
   feature fails, and how to balance errors *within* groups.
3. **[Fair kernel learning](03-fair-kernel-learning.qmd)** — linear neutrality
   and its hole, the Gaussianize-first trap (and the conditional fix), the CKA
   penalty hero — trained end to end with `keras-fairkl` — adversarial removal,
   and the accuracy-vs-neutrality frontier with its elbow.
4. **[Tie-back: (in)dependence and information](04-tie-back.qmd)** — fairness as
   the mirror of measurement; the two roads, once more.

The hands-on [labs](labs/index.qmd) build each rung in isolation, then neutralize
a real credit model and a real trading strategy.
